scope: Two OpenMS4 benchmark blockers of the mzML reader. (1) Source-compatible reading of a run startTimeStamp or processingMethod completion time that DateTime::set rejects, including the ProteoWizard sentinel "-infinity" and the Boost spellings "infinity" and "not-a-date-time". The executed source is lenient unconditionally, so mzml::ReadOptions::source_invalid_timestamps defaults to true and every TOPP tool reads such a file; a caller can set it to false to keep the refusal. (2) Size-derived cumulative reader ceilings: every cumulative allowance is floor + units * (consumed XML bytes / per_bytes), applied together with the absolute ReadOptions/LoadOptions ceilings, which default to unbounded. Records, binary arrays and parameter groups scale once per group of consumed bytes; the per-array byte ceiling stays absolute at 64 MiB. The Numpress coder allowance becomes per array; the scientific selection allowance stays cumulative but scales.

source_anchors.operation: DateTime::set throws Exception::ParseError for text no format matches, the sentinels included; the type has no notion of a sentinel, so the leniency belongs at the mzML boundary

asDateTime_: trims, keeps the first 19 characters, calls DateTime::set, catches ParseError, calls error(LOAD, 'DateTime conversion error of ...') and returns an unset DateTime; an empty string returns unset silently
error(LOAD, msg) prints 'Non-fatal error while loading ...' on OPENMS_LOG_ERROR and returns; loading continues
cvParamToValue, XSD_DATE branch: a value DateTime::set rejects warns and returns DataValue::EMPTY, so handleCVParam_ (MzMLHandler.cpp:1539) returns before the completion time is stored
run: exp_->setDateTime(asDateTime_(start_time)); the raw text is kept as mzml_start_time_stamp only when longer than 19 characters
writer: startTimeStamp is emitted only when the run DateTime is valid, and mzml_start_time_stamp is excluded from the run userParams (line 5229)
contrast for the ceilings: the source reserves from the declared list count and has no resource ceiling of any kind

external_reference_note: No C++ is committed to this repository. The C++ driver is a shell script under ../oracle/mzml-reader-scale/ that runs the prebuilt Release TOPP tools at /ceph/ibmi/abi/oliver/opt/openms4-release-bc9cc12-c19e494-174b576 (BUILD_MANIFEST.json there records the build); only its results enter the repository, as the oracle TSV above. The benchmark inputs stay on /ceph/ibmi/abi/oliver/bench/openms4/inputs and are read only by #[ignore]d tests.
method: Tier 1: datetime_sentinel_cpp.sh replaced run/@startTimeStamp in a three-spectrum slice of 50amol_R1.mzML with -infinity, infinity, not-a-date-time, an empty value and a valid control, added a processingMethod completion time of not-a-date-time in a sixth case, and ran the C++ Release FileInfo, FileConverter and MzMLSplitter on each. Exit codes, stderr and the written run element are the expected values in tests/mzml_reader_scale.rs. Tier 4: an instrumented reader with every ceiling disabled measured the charge of each cumulative allowance per consumed XML byte on all six benchmark mzML inputs (0.5-2.3 GB, uncompressed and zlib); the InputScaling defaults keep the former fixed ceilings as floors and grant at least eight times the largest measured ratio per byte. The #[ignore]d HPC tests then read every input with the defaults and compare spectrum counts against inputs/MANIFEST.json, which a Python header scan produced. Synthetic documents (20,000 sparse spectra; 4,000 zlib and 6,500 Numpress spectra of 200-500 points) show that the former fixed ceilings, reproduced by InputScaling::fixed, reject a realistic file while the size-derived ones admit it, and adversarial documents (a declared billion points, a 4,000-fold zlib bomb, a 20,000-parameter group expanded per spectrum, 200 levels of nesting) stay refused. Round 2: the completion-time case was re-executed on the Debug product SDK, which prints the warning the Release build suppresses (XMLHandler::warning is OPENMS_LOG_WARN only under OPENMS_ASSERTIONS), so the port's second warning line is source behaviour and not an invention; the timestamp default was changed to the source behaviour, which is unconditional there, and proved at tool level on ibminode06 (MapNormalizer and DTAExtractor exit 0 on the -infinity slice, where the previous round's binaries exited 6). The per-array ceiling was returned to 64 MiB after counting the largest array in every benchmark input directly (53,824 elements, 431 KB decoded, 155x inside it), and records, binary arrays and parameter groups received their own size-derived allowances from the measured densities (one record per 3,951 bytes and one array per 3,559 in the densest input, granted one per 512 and one per 256).

Tool-level runs are in tool_probe_ibminode06.log and tool_probe2_ibminode06.log, and the direct record/array counts in array_scan_ibminode06.log.
